Some good news out of Missouri last week.
First, some context: last year, the [legislature referred an amendment](https://substack.com/redirect/77c879f5-53a4-452a-8103-c237c744d97a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the voters that would make it functionally impossible1 for voter-initiated ballot measures2 to become part of the state constitution.
The legislature knows that this sort of thing wouldn't be popular--[North Dakota](https://substack.com/redirect/e4b8b325-5fb2-4b0b-8d22-d3bac9a1add1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Ohio](https://substack.com/redirect/d8053755-abda-44bc-9e06-4f150021437f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and others have tried this without success--so the legislature did what they've done before: they included some "ballot candy."
What that means is that the legislature paired what it actually wanted to do--make it all but impossible for citizen-initiated ballot measures to pass--with some super popular policies to hide its true intentions and sneak a seismic change past unsuspecting voters. **Confusion and deceit were the goals**.
Here's what the amendment originally said. You don't even get to the important part until the fourth bullet:
> Shall the Missouri Constitution be amended to:
> * Stop foreign nationals and foreign adversaries of the United States from providing funding to influence ballot measure elections, and allow criminal prosecution of violators;
> * Punish initiative petition signature fraud as a crime;
> * Require public hearings be held to get public comment before initiative petitions are placed on the ballot;
> * Require a majority of voters in each congressional district to approve initiative petitions to amend the constitution; and
> * Make available to each voter the full text of initiative petitions with their ballot?
>

Anyway, the good news: a judge in Missouri3 [ruled that the legislature can't do this](https://substack.com/redirect/5d12dd9b-ab2c-49ae-a80b-b002c63fb1bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), because they're just restating existing law. The ruling makes it much likelier that voters will defeat this ballot measure, which would strip away a [right that Missourians have had since 1908](https://substack.com/redirect/b50fe9f8-e593-46d3-b960-fc4bf5ecef1f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). But it's a continuation of an alarming trend in Republican states all over the country:
1. Legislators are unwilling (or unable) to pass laws that voters want.
2. Voters, using the rights they have to initiate and pass ballot measures, make changes to their state laws and state constitutions.
3. Legislators--because they're unhappy with the laws that are passed, uncompromising ideologues, and/or convinced they know what's better for voters than the voters themselves do--try to strip those rights away, often dismissing the voters as [misled](https://substack.com/redirect/bb6b4cb3-a029-4c88-a17f-b7ac0e24beef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) or [uninformed](https://substack.com/redirect/8e48d686-a1ad-4d8f-a9fc-f9ebaafa4da4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) or [confused](https://substack.com/redirect/51b4cf7a-1ef3-4e08-8f28-1c5e786cb77a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

There are lots of concurrent threats to democracy happening right now. We need to focus more on this one.
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9iZW5zYW11ZWxzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9hY2NvdW50IiwicCI6MTg4NzM3NzI4LCJzIjoyNDQwMzk4LCJmIjp0cnVlLCJ1Ijo5MDUwMTE5MiwiaWF0IjoxNzcyMDMxMzkwLCJleHAiOjIwODc2MDczOTAsImlzcyI6InB1Yi0wIiwic3ViIjoibGluay1yZWRpcmVjdCJ9.C6-dox9Aowk4z-kkbI0rIWckP9xgtSxq5Tpe8JVqlTs?)
### A (brief) history of ballot measures and direct democracy
Most laws in this country get passed because they're voted on by our elected legislators. Ballot measures, a type of direct democracy, allow voters to directly vote on specific policies, bypassing legislatures4 to enshrine things into law.
Ballot measures are not part of the U.S. Constitution or the federal government at all. That's not a surprise; although the U.S. has (generally) gotten more small-d democratic over time,5 it's still exceedingly difficult to amend the U.S. Constitution.
But on the state level, constitutions are much easier to amend. And for a variety of reasons--the [Progressive movement](https://substack.com/redirect/9bfc7253-992a-4825-9d2a-c408c93e3d38?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of the early 1900s, the [temperance movement](https://substack.com/redirect/1202c6e6-e57d-49ed-aa12-dd779aaa4d27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), organized labor, corruption scandals--voters elected legislators who advanced direct democracy.6 Between 1898 and 1918, [26 states added some right to initiate and/or pass ballot measures](https://substack.com/redirect/0696e5b0-6e95-4e91-abd1-7b2b92b5ce75?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), including Missouri.
Ballot measures are imperfect--more on that below--but they're generally good. That's especially true for issues like gerrymandering, where as I've written before, [the incentives of legislators are structurally misaligned](https://substack.com/redirect/b0542531-d91f-419a-b200-de2bdb5baf13?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with what voters want.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/0a6b3e60-3fb4-48a6-a914-5dd868b189ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [America's Coalition of Losers](https://substack.com/redirect/0a6b3e60-3fb4-48a6-a914-5dd868b189ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [Ben Samuels](https://substack.com/profile/12425779-ben-samuels)| | *
---|---|---
| November 12, 2025
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/0a6b3e60-3fb4-48a6-a914-5dd868b189ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But Republican governors and legislators don't like what their voters are passing.7 And over the past few years, they've been trying hard to whittle away these rights or to strip them from voters entirely.
It's the most concerted attack on ballot measures in more than a century.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=188737728&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg4NzM3NzI4LCJpYXQiOjE3NzIwMzEzOTAsImV4cCI6MTc3NDYyMzM5MCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.88CgHoRSa6sC37lk12vL3-hfJSXu6U9pJzsWgmXLrS4)
### Republican states are rolling back these rights
At an alarming pace, elected Republicans are trying to make it harder--or impossible--to pass ballot measures. Here's a non-exhaustive list of attempts in Republican states to make ballot measures harder:
* _**Arkansas**_ : [wholesale rejecting proposed amendments](https://substack.com/redirect/ca1864de-8ba1-4f51-a4ff-c320bfc1c26d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) without the authority to do so (2024); [rejecting petition signatures](https://substack.com/redirect/5146e7e7-ecb5-4b28-8e5f-c643620d4adc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) under murky circumstances (2024); allowing the legislature to [repeal citizen-initiated amendments](https://substack.com/redirect/cf59e908-fc4e-4706-ac72-743a4d163602?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (2025).
* _**Florida**_ : changing the rules to [make signature gathering prohibitively difficult](https://substack.com/redirect/3d97fce9-5914-4039-ba19-0058c1cc05e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (2025).
* _**Idaho**_ : [Changing signature-gathering requirements](https://substack.com/redirect/929ba1f7-2444-4fbc-a650-0f1b87111018?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) such that it would be "nearly impossible to bring a ballot initiative or referendum forward" (2021).
* _**Missouri**_ : [Referring a constitutional amendment with biased language](https://substack.com/redirect/4aca289e-b21f-46f9-944e-f5337304c685?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to repeal nonpartisan redistricting, one election after [Missourians voted to end partisan gerrymandering](https://substack.com/redirect/4208f381-bf2f-4e57-b8ef-7fa8421b55f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (2020); giving a pro-abortion access ballot measure [plainly misleading language](https://substack.com/redirect/e84da03d-6892-4b2c-bfbe-cc821b9f54c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (2023); in the subsequent election, [referring an amendment to repeal abortion access](https://substack.com/redirect/379b3e94-e9ad-4710-a139-87308abface7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), again with misleading language (2025); [repealing sick leave protections that voters approved](https://substack.com/redirect/c2c819a4-b967-4c03-aead-51bc2d512602?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) just months prior (2025); [referring an amendment to repeal expanded Medicaid benefits](https://substack.com/redirect/3ff62a89-421d-480a-b9a8-68cef5733317?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) approved by voters (2026); everything outlined at the beginning of the article.8
* _**Montana**_ : [Adding the highest-in-the-nation fees](https://substack.com/redirect/04a56ed6-eb64-42b9-89ff-d8d8db3977e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in order to start gathering petition signatures (2023); giving [sweeping authority to the state attorney general](https://substack.com/redirect/613ce54b-f8ef-49d2-a806-482aeab32b8a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to reject or rewrite ballot language (2023).
* _**North Dakota**_ : [Making it harder to pass amendments](https://substack.com/redirect/c997db30-556f-41fc-a8c0-2a6f2edaf4e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by increasing the signature threshold and requiring voters to approve ballot measures in successive elections (2024).
* _**Ohio**_ : [Drafting deceptive language](https://substack.com/redirect/b6a787a9-16ec-459b-9fb9-078fca5edacd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for an abortion-access ballot measure (2023); [requiring a 60% threshold to pass](https://substack.com/redirect/dd009a0e-5f5a-4491-8010-9695e76994de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (rather than 50%) to make future amendments less likely (2023); [drafting deceptive language](https://substack.com/redirect/6629be35-ce84-40eb-9d41-1dcd72cb1663?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for a nonpartisan redistricting ballot measure (2024).
* _**Oklahoma**_ : [Reducing the number of petition signatures that can come from high-population counties](https://substack.com/redirect/ad55f5b8-49fb-4688-88a4-d62f634adb16?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which makes qualification meaningfully harder (2025).
* _**Utah**_ : [Delaying (for the better part of a decade) the rollout](https://substack.com/redirect/1df4288e-1b2d-46e8-89a9-9e55cdff2f2c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of nonpartisan redistricting [approved by voters](https://substack.com/redirect/e755f7cd-6885-45b9-b8d1-d34f87101bc8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (2026).

Some of these are in effect; some died because voters shot them down; some were overturned by courts; some never made it to voters. But it paints a clear picture of what they're trying.
### When it comes to ballot measures, nothing is more absurd than Mississippi
Mississippians, in theory, have the right to propose and pass their own ballot measures. To qualify, [petitioners need to gather signatures in at least five](https://substack.com/redirect/b9562d5f-6a25-420c-a1a9-b76f9bca9ed0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of the state's Congressional districts.
The problem? Since 2001, [Mississippi has only had four Congressional districts](https://substack.com/redirect/d97c2e16-b6bf-4820-8c97-c6b8ef4bbb14?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). In the other states, with proposed changes it's still _theoretically_ possible to qualify for the ballot. But not in Mississippi.
This absurdity went to the [Mississippi Supreme Court](https://substack.com/redirect/88eec4a1-8316-40a5-b165-8dd69b3ba9ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), who said, basically, that [they don't have the power to change anything](https://substack.com/redirect/20f3ecbe-4de6-4f4a-9be9-3872a8c52f05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).9 That ruling was back in 2021. Mississippi's legislature has had four chances (and counting) to fix this, but [they've chosen not to](https://substack.com/redirect/dc8065a3-c617-4fd7-abfa-49921c9521e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Notwithstanding Mississippi, to date, most Republican efforts in other states haven't succeeded, because voters don't like giving up their own power. But Republican states are trying different tactics, and eventually--without proactive reforms--something will stick.
It's worth noting: this is not a both sides issue. [I](https://substack.com/redirect/6a76d3b5-c402-4aa6-82be-35701fd01c4e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [have](https://substack.com/redirect/846a37a4-37da-4627-9b28-d97ac2b1dbb3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [no](https://substack.com/redirect/78c76489-0ac2-4296-ade6-12c94e440dc7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [problem](https://substack.com/redirect/2c7fcfcb-74af-41fa-b281-c4ce15fc7214?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [calling](https://substack.com/redirect/79d48aa2-d80f-4044-9df1-35e551f90f57?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [out](https://substack.com/redirect/cccc1f01-66e8-4067-ae33-3faea81b2695?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [Democrats](https://substack.com/redirect/6ceb40e3-dfc0-4e56-bf91-38698b29ee25?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [when](https://substack.com/redirect/a102e56d-c627-41be-9e96-ef30166c9cce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [they're in](https://substack.com/redirect/6ba58f97-1ecd-4cba-ae48-80690da2c61f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [the wrong](https://substack.com/redirect/bd626324-8b47-4e63-a60d-e7c83bc2d90f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).10 But the **systematic whittling away of this right is overwhelmingly happening in Republican states**.

### Direct democracy isn't perfect. That doesn't mean we should kill it
I've written--[extensively](https://substack.com/redirect/16f0b839-0cd3-4c03-9bd8-b82f3934e956?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--about how bad online sports gambling is for Missouri. But that was [added to the state constitution via ballot measure](https://substack.com/redirect/6699f4d8-c2ab-4da0-a62d-0a75fc7354a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the same way that it was legalized in [Colorado](https://substack.com/redirect/50e2fe28-5f32-45b2-aba2-41c35a607bcd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and the same way that sports gambling more generally was legalized in states like [Arkansas](https://substack.com/redirect/3719cb35-d47e-4b79-9f94-cea2e62aa65b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [Maryland](https://substack.com/redirect/4ae4a081-968d-47fc-95e0-8562ff4752bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).11
Voters have passed plenty of other bad policies at the ballot.12 So why keep it?
1. It's not like our legislatures (state or federal) have a track record of passing perfect laws.
2. Our legislatures aren't exactly doing much. As I wrote last year, the [Missouri legislature is passing fewer and fewer laws](https://substack.com/redirect/e568629a-9f24-445e-a9ca-3a2f7787c048?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Increasingly, it feels like some policy change _has_ to come from voters.
3. It's an important check on the power of state legislatures, especially given the intense gerrymandering that exists in state legislative districts. In the [2024 North Carolina House elections](https://substack.com/redirect/e800726d-e2dd-4e4f-9bad-bb7e864256ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), for example, Democrats won 51% of the statewide vote but hold only 41% of the seats because of gerrymandering.13 **Ballot measures are a safeguard against legislatures whose composition, because of gerrymandering, doesn 't align with the policies and values of its voters**.

### Ballot measures _do_ need reform
Part of the reason that Amendment 2 passed in Missouri to legalize online sports gambling is that [DraftKings and FanDuel each spent more than $20 million](https://substack.com/redirect/74625ce7-7df5-42e1-82a8-9df6cc2afc2c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on the race, outspending the opposition by a 4.5-to-1 margin.
If you're running for State House or State Senate in Missouri, [your donors are capped](https://substack.com/redirect/aa4c568f-75a7-4118-a1c6-15887cfdf881?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at a $2,400 donation per election, and corporations cannot give money to your campaign. But those rules don't apply to ballot measures; **there is no limit on how much donors can give** , and there are few rules on who's allowed to give.
This isn't unique to Missouri, by the way. [Alaska](https://substack.com/redirect/a6354b61-a250-426b-b65d-04d00e3b1080?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [California](https://substack.com/redirect/78977058-eccd-4077-95e3-570c4eb0048b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Indiana](https://substack.com/redirect/58dafd7a-e1f4-47b0-b31b-3fda0664d16d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [North Dakota](https://substack.com/redirect/143adfdb-dd9d-4c8a-87c5-c1e860e2c86d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Montana](https://substack.com/redirect/0ca9b3e3-b761-42fb-bca8-ef85954eefc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Nebraska](https://substack.com/redirect/02950e06-0566-45dd-8b47-135ad6c46c98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [New Jersey](https://substack.com/redirect/d80c5fbc-9b19-4d83-be9f-b2012b6d78d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Ohio](https://substack.com/redirect/83162c65-f15a-463d-858e-bc52979475ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Oklahoma](https://substack.com/redirect/d75c8196-d2a5-4092-8902-7848eefee471?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [South Dakota](https://substack.com/redirect/f48fa4e4-5d83-43e3-91c2-b2a4e53ff32a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Tennessee](https://substack.com/redirect/c181665b-dee4-4acb-9422-87052b79bb5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [Wyoming](https://substack.com/redirect/efcb0fb6-fc9a-44d2-b0f9-994f1a9e44d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) also have no contribution limits, and this isn't even an exhaustive list.14
Missouri's partisan Secretary of State is responsible for writing the ballot language that voters see,15 and that needs to change too. [Denny Hoskins](https://substack.com/redirect/e26ef6ab-1ad1-4bf2-9966-6930277fdfff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Missouri's [nutty Secretary of State](https://substack.com/redirect/162dc776-4495-4432-8bbb-22e4625b4e2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), is particularly shameless and egregious in the way that he approaches this duty.
In Missouri and other states, **there are efforts underway to protect ballot measures and keep partisan actors from writing unfair or actively misleading ballot language**. This, along with campaign contribution limits, are two sensible reforms that voters can (for now) pass via ballot measure.
It's an unfortunate state of affairs that we need ballot measures to protect ballot measures.

### Democrats should be careful with how they talk about democracy issues
A few weeks ago, the [U.S. House passed the SAVE Act](https://substack.com/redirect/8dbc3625-af34-48ed-8b6b-be8314438281?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and it's been a hot partisan issue since then. I object to the bill mostly because it addresses a made-up problem; [voter fraud is virtually nonexistent](https://substack.com/redirect/5dd61faf-4603-4f2d-ab18-99b6e16522cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the U.S.
Even if it were to pass, and [prediction markets think that's unlikely](https://substack.com/redirect/1438ec9f-60ad-461b-a8c0-a4e6b77576a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg),16 it's not totally obvious that Democrats would be hurt by it any more than Republicans.17 The other thing about the SAVE Act: picking this fight may not be a political winner for Democrats.
The bill is about more than just voter ID, but [84% of Americans support voter ID laws](https://substack.com/redirect/c2151eaf-68a7-481b-8561-a2a8df3b2226?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). If it gets framed as such, and [I think it will](https://substack.com/redirect/85f4b79c-5590-473b-868c-a7eb81567979?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), fighting this in the court of public opinion isn't a winner.
But fighting against Republican states limiting the rights of voters? That's a political winner. This one is pressing, urgent, and easy to understand. It's a war worth waging.

I've got my [well-established issues with prediction markets](https://substack.com/redirect/d078ddd4-2ba6-4758-a50d-8b36ce838c12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but their pricing is generally rational and a good way to look at the odds that something will or won't happen. That doesn't mean that they should exist, and it certainly doesn't mean that they should exist with basically zero regulation.
17
This was a [good ](https://substack.com/redirect/502aeded-85bb-4549-9f99-801a72ac83b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[Washington Post](https://substack.com/redirect/502aeded-85bb-4549-9f99-801a72ac83b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ op-ed on the topic](https://substack.com/redirect/502aeded-85bb-4549-9f99-801a72ac83b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from a few weeks ago. But even beyond that, [analysis suggests](https://substack.com/redirect/667a1f50-46dd-434e-890f-80e197f660ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that younger people (predominantly Democratic) _and_ [older people](https://substack.com/redirect/667a1f50-46dd-434e-890f-80e197f660ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (predominantly Republican) would be hurt by this bill. [Communities of color](https://substack.com/redirect/bcd3ef72-ae70-4e26-9734-e4971876650a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (who lean Democratic) would be hurt by the bill, but [so would rural Americans](https://substack.com/redirect/79a859c1-b6c1-4f39-8a4c-fc64ee0c18f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (who lean Republican).
In short: it's not clear who would benefit from this bill passing, but what's clear is that it's addressing a problem that doesn't exist.

They put Ashley Moody in the Senate to be a ‘yes’ vote for Trump and the billionaires. She’s not Florida’s senator. She’s theirs.
We need someone who isn’t afraid to put a check on an outlaw president, to defend our democracy, and to make sure that every American has a fair chance at prosperity.

CHIP IN TODAY TO HELP DEMS FLIP THE SENATE! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vindman]
The billionaires and special interests will throw everything they’ve got to try and stop us. But in the infantry, we didn’t back down from a fight — we went towards it. Join me.
Thank you.
Alex Vindman

Last night, President Donald Trump addressed a joint session of Congress for 1 hour and 47 minutes--the longest State of the Union address on record--and declared that the United States is living through "the golden age of America." Invoking the nation's upcoming 250th anniversary, he framed his first year back in office as nothing less than "a turnaround for the ages." Based on [polling](https://substack.com/redirect/da41bd9e-c915-481f-9668-cfdf153df637?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), many people would disagree. His approval rating sits at 36%, with the midterms a little more than seven months away.
Surprisingly, Trump did not give much focus to world issues, instead focusing on the issues at home like affordability, energy, and manufacturing.
Here are some of the main highlights from his speech.
## Venezuela
Trump opened his foreign-policy remarks with Venezuela, calling it "our new friend and partner" after the dramatic U.S. operation to seize Nicolas Maduro, along with his wife and son from Caracas. He called the capture a "colossal victory for the United States" and a "bright new beginning for the people of Venezuela," and separately touted the flow of 80 million barrels of Venezuelan oil into the U.S.
What he didn't mention were the military strikes on vessels suspected of smuggling drugs that have [killed more than 150 people](https://substack.com/redirect/0297eeb2-c5f2-4125-8c5c-dbc9f32b153f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) since September, operations legal experts have widely condemned as unlawful. Congress has sat quietly on the sidelines about this.
## Russia-Ukraine
On the fourth anniversary of Russia's invasion of Ukraine, Trump gave just a passing mention to the war. He repeated his claim that it never would have happened if he'd been president.

He completely omitted his vision for what America's position will be going forward. On the campaign trail he had promised the war would be over on Day One. Instead, Russia controls nearly 1/5th of Ukraine and the fighting has continued. Ukraine has suffered [500,000 casualties](https://substack.com/redirect/b335d94b-75b4-4845-8b90-0ff763333bbd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but has been roughly stalemated by the iron will of their people, with [Russia suffering over 1.2 million casualties](https://substack.com/redirect/39da4c7a-a994-4ed6-892c-1d9b151e3e2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of their own.
There was no articulation of strategy or clarity about whether the United States intends to deepen its support for Ukraine and push for negotiations, condition aid, or redraw the terms of engagement altogether.
## Iran
Trump also devoted surprisingly little time to Iran, which is striking, given that U.S. forces are on standby amid the possibility of an attack with the USS Abraham Lincoln & USS George H.W. Bush carrier groups deployed to the region.
Instead, he touted "Operation Midnight Hammer," the summer strikes that partially took out Iran's three biggest uranium enrichment sites in Natanz, Fordow, and Isfahan. He reminded the chamber that the Iranian regime had killed 32,000 of its own protesters but gave no assurance or clarity for what America's position will be.
It's unclear what his goal is. Is it regime change or a permanent dismantling of their nuclear program? In a speech about projecting American strength, there was a missed opportunity to define what success actually looks like against one of the most formidable geopolitical threats on the board. Again, Congress clapped but refuses to exercise their enumerated constitutional powers and punts it silently over to the executive branch.

## Israel-Gaza
Trump touted the ceasefire between Israel and Hamas and the return of the remaining hostages after two years of war. Bringing the hostages home was one of his big campaign promises he delivered on ([I wrote about that here](https://substack.com/redirect/6a98699f-7a1e-496e-8600-ea22ec70fdfd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)). But beyond that, he offered no reassurance for what comes next.
He spoke as though the conflict was settled, which it isn't. There was no discussion of reconstruction, no outline of a credible path toward Israeli-Palestinian peace, no mention of his newly announced "Board of Peace." He didn't address the question of disarming Hamas. Nor did he explain what Phase 2 of his own peace plan actually looks like or how he intends to achieve it.
## Tariffs
Perhaps most notable in Trump's speech was how incensed he was over the Supreme Court ruling against his emergency tariffs.
Trump called the ruling "unfortunate" and "totally wrong," publicly humiliating the justices to their face as they sat in the first row, a few yards away. Somehow, the justices all remained stoic and didn't flinch.

He also repeated a false claim that tariffs are "paid for by foreign countries" and will one day "substantially replace the modern-day system of income tax." That framing glosses over a basic fact: tariffs are paid by American importers, who often pass those costs on to consumers with an average cost of $1200 paid per American family. (You can find my recent [Substack on the Supreme Court's tariff decision](https://substack.com/redirect/10353e32-1426-4338-a6c0-c35316498151?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) here).

Trump signaled he is not done. He suggested he will turn to other statutory authorities to continue imposing tariffs, "leading to a solution that will be even stronger than before." But other statutes like Section 122 only authorize these for 150 days, so let's see if Congress springs to action.
## Medicaid
Trump promised to always protect Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid. The first two he's largely kept faith with. The third... not so much. His signature legislation passed last summer cut more than $1 trillion from Medicaid over the next decade, the largest reduction in the program's history. It's expected to push over 10 million people off the rolls through tighter eligibility requirements and new work mandates.
## Voter Fraud
Trump once again falsely claimed that cheating in American elections is "rampant," and accused Democrats of relying on fraud because their "policy is so bad." He suggested he should effectively be serving a third term, rooted in his long-standing claim that the 2020 election was stolen from him.
He went further, announcing his intention to end most forms of mail-in voting, limiting it to narrow exceptions such as disability, military service, illness, or travel.
There is little evidence of widespread voter fraud in modern American elections. Courts, state officials from both parties, and numerous audits have consistently found no proof of the kind of systemic cheating the president describes. Questioning the legitimacy of elections signals that the fight over this (non) issue is far from over.
## Economy
Trump said "A year ago we were a dead country. Now we're the hottest country anywhere in the world."
The economy grew [2.2% in 2025](https://substack.com/redirect/56285162-c223-4ded-9b19-d02f3b220a70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (after growing 2.8% in 2024), which is neither dead nor scorching hot. Most of that growth came from AI investment rather than the kind of broad, working-class expansion he has championed. Job creation dropped from 1.5 million in 2024 to 200,000 this past year. Unemployment has climbed to 4.4%. Consumer confidence fell 33%, near historic lows. Inflation still sits around 2.7% (after being 2.9% in 2024).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/930b3560-cb10-4103-a8db-d7ee1a204cdf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
## Inflation
Trump claimed he inherited record inflation from Biden and brought it way down, neither of which is true. Inflation peaked for one month at around [9% in June 2022](https://substack.com/redirect/a86d3ae9-5cfb-4f2a-b851-3edf8e5d320c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- a four-decade high, but not an all-time record; the 1970s and 1980s were worse. For the full year, inflation averaged roughly 8%, and the Federal Reserve implemented aggressive monetary tightening to bring it down. By the time Trump took office in January 2025, it had already fallen to [2.9%](https://substack.com/redirect/a4dd39db-747d-472f-a594-6e79e257e02c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Trump praised core inflation for coming down, which is technically correct. But core inflation and what people pay for groceries are different things, and most Americans experience the latter.
He also claimed that grocery prices have come down, when they haven't, with the exceptions of eggs and beef. Overall food prices are up 2.1% over the past year, and food-price inflation has actually picked up since Trump returned to office. December saw a 0.7% single-month jump in grocery prices, the largest since October 2022.
But increased government spending increases inflation - last year the federal government spent $7 trillion while running up a $1.7 trillion deficit. Adding to our $38 trillion national debt is handcuffing future generations that past Chairmen of the Joint Chiefs have called the biggest national security threat to the United States (but both parties in Congress have generally ignored).
## Some Good
Trump hailed the rollout of "Trump Accounts," tax-free savings accounts for American children seeded by a $6 billion gift from Michael Dell. He said the funding would cover 25 million accounts that, if invested over time, could grow to more than $100,000 by the time those children turn 18.
Later in the evening, the men's Olympic hockey team entered the chamber draped in gold medals to chants of "USA," a moment of unbridled patriotism that drew the loudest applause of the night.
Toward the end of the evening, 100-year-old combat veteran Capt. E. [Royce Williams](https://substack.com/redirect/33ce6853-1069-447c-925f-1d9a1120b93b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was recognized as his Navy Cross was formally upgraded to the Medal of Honor, the nation's highest military award. A decorated Navy aviator, Williams first served with distinction in World War II and later flew missions during the Korean and Vietnam Wars. He will turn 101 on April 4.

A Medal of Honor was also awarded to Army Chief Warrant Officer 5 [Eric Slover](https://substack.com/redirect/8a03530d-56a3-4265-9e0d-3a7c437427a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a helicopter pilot wounded during the high-risk raid that led to the capture of Nicolas Maduro in January. Slover was flying the lead CH-47 Chinook when it came under heavy fire, sustaining multiple gunshot wounds while keeping the aircraft steady enough for the mission to continue.
## **Your Thoughts?**
Overall, Trump's speech was fairly unrevealing in what his plans are aside from more tariffs. Watching the analysis afterwards, Trump Republicans loved it and partisan Democrats hated it. The battle in the midterms and federal elections really comes down to Independents - which broke for Trump in 2016, not 2020, but then again for him in 2024. What did you think?

Toward the end of the evening, 100-year-old combat veteran Capt. E. was recognized as his Navy Cross was formally upgraded to the Medal of Honor, the nation's highest military award. A decorated Navy aviator, Williams first served with distinction in World War II and later flew missions during the Korean and Vietnam Wars. He will turn 101 on April 4. A Medal of Honor was also awarded to Army Chief Warrant Officer 5 , a helicopter pilot wounded during the high-risk raid that led to the capture of Nicolas Maduro in January. Slover was flying the lead CH-47 Chinook when it came under heavy fire, sustaining multiple gunshot wounds while keeping the aircraft steady enough for the mission to continue. Your Thoughts?** Overall, Trump's speech was fairly unrevealing in what his plans are aside from more tariffs. Watching the analysis afterwards, Trump Republicans loved it and partisan Democrats hated it. The battle in the midterms and federal elections really comes down to Independents - which broke for Trump in 2016, not 2020, but then again for him in 2024. What did you think? Share your comments below. I'd love to hear what you think. If you appreciate my commentary on these issues, please consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. name: Anika Page
subject: Dispatch from the Dome: Strengthening Private Support for Mississippi Families
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/dome-dispatch-12852216?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| Good morning Friend,
This week at the Capitol has been quieter on major headline legislation, but that doesn’t mean meaningful policy conversations aren’t happening. One bill worth highlighting right now is **HB 1944** — a proposal that focuses on strengthening private support for Mississippi families and nonprofit organizations serving vulnerable communities. Here’s what it does — and why it matters.
---
|
### **What HB 1944 Would Do**
HB 1944 proposes expanding Mississippi’s existing tax credit structure for certain charitable contributions. In simple terms, the bill would increase the amount of tax credits available to businesses that contribute to qualifying nonprofit organizations — including those that provide services for children in foster care and other educational or support programs. Rather than expanding government programs, this approach encourages **private investment** in community-based organizations that are already doing critical work across our state. It’s a policy model rooted in a simple principle: when the private sector and nonprofit community are empowered, families benefit.
---
|
### **Why This Matters**
Mississippi has no shortage of organizations stepping in to serve children, support struggling families, and strengthen communities. Many of these groups operate on tight budgets and rely heavily on private donations. By expanding tax incentives for charitable giving, HB 1944 aims to:
* Encourage additional private-sector support
* Strengthen the capacity of nonprofits serving vulnerable populations
* And reduce reliance on expanding state bureaucracy

It’s not a sweeping reform bill — but it reflects an important policy approach: supporting solutions that flow through civil society rather than exclusively through government expansion.
---
|
### **What Comes Next**
HB 1944 is currently moving through the legislative process and will continue to be evaluated in committee. As with any tax policy change, lawmakers will weigh its fiscal impact alongside its potential community benefit. We’ll continue monitoring its progress and evaluating how it fits within broader conversations about tax policy, charitable giving, and support for Mississippi families.
---
|
### **Looking Ahead**
Not every week at the Capitol is defined by high-profile floor fights. Sometimes progress shows up in targeted policy adjustments that strengthen institutions outside of government. As always, I’ll keep breaking down what’s moving — and what’s not — in plain language. If you’d like to follow legislation in real time, you can track bills throughout the session using the Mississippi Center for Public Policy’s bill tracker.
---
| [Track Bills at the Capitol](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=13d5dbf037&e=5703353baa "Track Bills at the Capitol")
---
| Thanks for staying engaged and informed. I’ll continue tracking these developments and keeping you updated as reform moves forward.
---
| |
---
Until next time,

Anika Page
Director of Operations

| | Fellow Patriot,

| | Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud.

He filled arenas. He lit a fire in the next generation on campus.

He confronted lies and spoke truth with boldness.

And he built a movement and a machine that few ever thought possible.

I saw it up close -- _Charlie moved at a pace most couldn 't keep up with. _

But in the middle of all the noise... he made a quiet decision that changed everything.

_**He started observing the Sabbath. **_

Not as a box to check. Not as a religious performance.

_But as an act of obedience. _

As a way of saying, **_" God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." _**

Every week -- no matter what -- Charlie stopped.

He turned off the noise. He stepped away from the battlefield.

No email. No media. No work.

He gave his full attention fully to God, his wife Erika, and his children.

It was hard at first -- for someone who carried so much.

But over time, it changed him.

And before he was assassinated, he wrote a book about what he had learned...

Fellow Patriot, like I mentioned, this isn't a political book.

It's not a culture war manifesto.

It's a call to stop.

To rest. To breathe. To return to God.

**Because Charlie believed America hadn 't just forgotten truth... It had forgotten trust. **

Trust that the world keeps spinning when you step away.

Trust that God is in control.

Trust that rest is not weakness -- it's worship.

**In _Stop, in the Name of God,_ you'll discover: **

🔥 How Charlie reclaimed the Sabbath in a world built on burnout

🔥 What sacred rest gave back to him -- as a father, husband, and believer

🔥 Why he believed this message could spark revival in a restless generation

Charlie wrote this book because he knew what it meant to nearly lose his peace -- and what it felt like to find it again.

That's the heartbeat of his final message.

clean_body: It wasn’t about politics... Charlie Kirk’s final message—receive his book when you give any amount to Turning Point USA. | | | | | Fellow Patriot, | | Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud. He filled arenas. He lit a fire in the next generation on campus. He confronted lies and spoke truth with boldness. And he built a movement and a machine that few ever thought possible. I saw it up close -- Charlie moved at a pace most couldn 't keep up with. But in the middle of all the noise... he made a quiet decision that changed everything. He started observing the Sabbath. Not as a box to check. Not as a religious performance. But as an act of obedience. As a way of saying, " God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." Every week -- no matter what -- Charlie stopped. He turned off the noise. He stepped away from the battlefield. No email. No media. No work. He gave his full attention fully to God, his wife Erika, and his children. It was hard at first -- for someone who carried so much. But over time, it changed him. And before he was assassinated, he wrote a book about what he had learned... This was Charlie's final message. His final act of trust. A book not about politics... but about peace. It 's called: Stop, in the Name of God. Fellow Patriot, like I mentioned, this isn't a political book. It's not a culture war manifesto. It's a call to stop. To rest. To breathe. To return to God. Because Charlie believed America hadn 't just forgotten truth... It had forgotten trust. Trust that the world keeps spinning when you step away. Trust that God is in control. Trust that rest is not weakness -- it's worship. In Stop, in the Name of God, you'll discover: 🔥 How Charlie reclaimed the Sabbath in a world built on burnout 🔥 What sacred rest gave back to him -- as a father, husband, and believer 🔥 Why he believed this message could spark revival in a restless generation Charlie wrote this book because he knew what it meant to nearly lose his peace -- and what it felt like to find it again. That's the heartbeat of his final message. Charlie Kirk didn't waste his time on earth. He left behind a family. He left behind a movement. And he left behind this truth... For anyone ready to step off the treadmill... and walk back toward what's eternal. Fellow Patriot, thank you -- in advance -- for helping reach the next generation with truth, faith, and moral courage. These are the very things Charlie gave his life for. May the message he left behind lead you -- just as it led him -- to a deeper trust in God... A stronger love for your family... And a renewed peace in your own soul. For Charlie, Justin Streiff Chief Operating Officer Turning Point USA P.S.Stop, in the Name of God is Charlie Kirk's final message -- written in obedience, shaped by Scripture, and grounded in trust in the Lord. 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044

Derek,
I delivered the Democratic Spanish language response to President Trump’s State of the Union address yesterday.
Because Americans didn’t need another speech from Donald Trump pretending everything is fine when their bills are too high, paychecks are too low, and masked and militarized federal agents are roaming our communities violating constitutional rights on a daily basis.
I refuse to accept the president’s failed economic agenda that makes billionaires richer while middle class Americans see their health care costs rise.
I refuse to accept a federal government that weaponizes federal agencies against immigrants and U.S. citizens alike.
And I refuse to accept attacks on the right to vote.
There is a better path — one that lowers costs, safeguards our democracy, and reins in rogue federal agencies. Americans demand and deserve accountability, stability, and a government that works for them.
But it is up to us to put in the work and build a better future for everyone. _Solo el pueblo salva al pueblo_. “Only the community saves the community.”
That’s what I discussed yesterday. It’s what Democrats are fighting for every day.**And it’s why we must take back the Senate, the House, and seats up and down the ballot this fall.**

Hi Peter,
Time and time again, this administration has been telling us to doubt what we have seen with our own eyes, so I felt that it was my duty to attend the State of the Union address last night to witness the challenges we are up against.
Trump’s cruelty knows no bounds. While everyday Minnesotans are stepping up to take care of each other and protect their neighbors from ICE, and the majority of Americans are struggling to afford their groceries, he falsely claimed that we are in the “golden age of America.”
Please, let me remind you:
Over the past year, the Trump administration has taken a wrecking ball to our healthcare system, pursued a chaotic and unconstitutional tariff war, sent federal troops into our cities, and is actively deteriorating our democracy. This administration’s policies are hurting working families and are terrorizing our communities. This administration has made us all less safe.
I did want to call out the President’s self-praise about his work on healthcare. Peter, in just one year, Trump has done significant damage to scientific and medical research in our country. Aided by his Republican majorities in Congress, he has also gutted Medicaid and made healthcare unaffordable for working Americans. This administration has spouted misinformation and undermined the nation's trust in vaccines, and we are now facing the worst measles outbreak in America since the year 2000. As a physician, I can confirm that this President’s policies are creating a crisis that will hurt all of us.
Peter, we cannot go on like this. We must flip the U.S. House of Representatives this November to provide some checks on this runaway administration. | | |

Hi Peter -- Over the weekend, the Portland Press Herald featured a two-page spread on our campaign asking a simple but important question: **Could Maine’s next Governor be an independent?**

I was honored by what so many Mainers shared and the consensus was clear: Yes!

One of those voices was Riley Worth, a 23-year-old recent USM graduate from Sabattus:

_“It’d be great to have someone at the state level who’s more focused on getting the job done rather than toeing the party line. There are so many great ideas Republicans have and so many great ideas Democrats have... I like that an independent can pick and choose from each.”_

That’s exactly why I’m running.

As an independent, I answer only to the people of Maine – not party bosses, not dark-money interests, and not DC operatives. That independence allows me to stay focused on what truly matters: making life more affordable, strengthening our economy, and restoring trust in government.

But independence only works when people step up together.

body:
I've been thinking about what Kansans needed to hear — and what was missing

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126104513/603923273/454992728?amounts=5,25,50,100,250,500,1000&refcode=email_022526_sotu&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NTc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1OWQ2N2U1ZC02MDEyLWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2E1NzU5M2YiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=SU72TcCFfDzgiRZCYsErDye4HgFTq_EauVsgDQTCVnY=) After listening to the President’s State of the Union last night, I’ve been thinking about what Kansans needed to hear — and what was missing. I didn’t hear a clear plan on how to help lower the cost of living for families here in KS-03. I didn’t hear meaningful acknowledgement of the financial pressure so many Kansans are under — from rising grocery bills to housing costs to prescription drugs. Instead, all I heard was divisive, dangerous, partisan rhetoric. **So if Donald Trump doesn’t want to acknowledge the pain families are feeling right now, I will:** Families are worried about making ends meet. Small businesses are navigating higher costs, and farmers and manufacturers are trying to plan for the future in the face of economic uncertainty. Affordable health care is out of reach. Our fundamental freedoms are under attack. Rampant government corruption has been left unchecked — just to name a few. Kansans deserve leadership focused on practical solutions — and that’s the work I’m committed to. But here’s the truth: National Republicans still haven’t given up on KS-03. They still believe — with enough money and enough attacks — they can take full control of Kansas’ Congressional delegation and expand their House majority. So if we want to keep fighting for Kansas families — and make sure real solutions break through Donald Trump’s noise — we need to win this race. subject: New Politics Endorses Eileen Laubacher for Congress in Colorado's 4th District
body:
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE:** Contact: Aly Ferguson[aly@newpolitics.org](mailto:aly@newpolitics.org); 480-363-6465
---
|
---
| | **NEW POLITICS ENDORSES EILEEN LAUBACHER FOR CONGRESS IN COLORADO'S 4TH DISTRICT****WASHINGTON D.C. (February 25, 2026) —** [New Politics](https://eileenforcolorado.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=400e8fa21dba23169b817268c&id=5677c44a05&e=1c5f08419c) today endorsed Rear Admiral (Ret.) Eileen Laubacher for U.S. Congress in Colorado's 4th Congressional District. A 34-year Navy veteran, Laubacher served as Defense Attaché to India and Senior Director for South Asia on the National Security Council, embodying the principled, mission-focused leadership that New Politics seeks to elevate.**Emily Cherniack, Founder and Executive Director of New Politics,** released the following statement:“Eileen Laubacher has dedicated her entire career to serving our country with distinction and honor. She has consistently put mission before self, rising through the ranks from intelligence officer to admiral and serving everywhere from New Delhi to the White House. In a moment when our democracy faces unprecedented threats, Eileen is answering the call to serve once more. Colorado's 4th District deserves serious leadership that puts constituents over corporate donors, and Eileen embodies exactly that. Her commitment to service and integrity is exactly what we need in Congress, and New Politics is honored to support her campaign.”**About Eileen Laubacher** Rear Admiral (Ret.) Eileen Laubacher is a 34-year U.S. Navy veteran who followed a proud family legacy of service. She joined the 11th class with women at the United States Naval Academy and graduated in 1990. After more than seven years as an intelligence officer serving in the United States and abroad, she left active duty and joined the Navy Reserve. She made Colorado home with her husband Chris and raised five children in Highlands Ranch, CO. In 2009, she deployed to Afghanistan when her children were 10, 8, 6, 4, and 1. When she became an Admiral in 2018, the Navy asked her to serve as Senior Defense Official and Defense Attaché in New Delhi, India from 2019 to 2022. After that tour, she was asked to join the National Security Council to serve as Senior Director for South Asia. She retired from the Navy in October 2024 and returned home to Colorado, where she lives with her husband, children, and three grandchildren. Learn more at [eileenforcolorado.com](https://eileenforcolorado.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=400e8fa21dba23169b817268c&id=22b7e11385&e=1c5f08419c).
**About New Politics** New Politics is an organization that revitalizes American democracy by recruiting, developing, and electing leaders across the ideological and political spectrum who have committed their lives to serving their communities and our country, either through military service, national service organizations like AmeriCorps or the Peace Corps, or by demonstrating strong service-based leadership in their community. New Politics support includes strategic advising and training in all aspects of a candidate’s campaign, such as fundraising, communications, organizing, hiring, and team building. New Politics has raised over $40 million to support over 475 candidates, successfully electing more than 200 of them to office, from Congress to School Board. Learn more at [newpolitics.org](https://eileenforcolorado.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=400e8fa21dba23169b817268c&id=65dcdd5c3a&e=1c5f08419c). **##**

body:
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
BCJ: Independent State Legislature Theory [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=022526_1&amount=25]
In 2023, the U.S. Supreme Court decided Moore v. Harper, which rejected the so-called "independent state legislature" (ISL) theory. In theory.
Now opponents of voting rights are revisiting this fringe legal theory to give state legislatures nearly unchecked authority to gerrymander electoral maps and pass voter suppression laws. Facing mounting setbacks to their nationwide gerrymanders, the vote suppressors are citing this fringe legal theory to block voter referendums, court-ordered maps, and other safeguards built into our democracy that may threaten their partisan electoral advantage.
This is all about the upcoming midterm elections. Voters and courts are pushing back against some egregious partisan and racial gerrymanders by striking down or threatening to block the use of those maps. In response, opponents of voting rights want to use this "independent state legislature" constitutional argument to sideline those very checks on their power.
In state after state, the battle is no longer just about how district lines are drawn, but about who gets a say in the process. Which is why we've got to inform voters about this theory and how to defend our fundamental right to vote before it's too late . The fate of mail-in ballots, early voting programs, 3rd party voter outreach, and so much more is at risk around the country.
Fuel our efforts to reach every voter possible ahead of November with $35 or whatever you can today and help increase voter participation nationwide >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=022526_1&amount=35]

Don't remember the ISL theory? You're not alone.
The ISL is a right-wing constitutional theory about who has the power to set rules for federal elections. The theory interprets the word “legislature” in the U.S. Constitution to mean that state legislatures — and only state legislatures — can make laws regulating federal elections. This differs from the standard interpretation, in which “legislature” means the state’s general lawmaking process, which includes the governor’s veto, citizen-led ballot measures and rulings of state courts.
We need to make sure that the role of the judiciary -- and voters -- in determining and protecting voting rights laws is upheld. The ISL could weaken long-standing, constitutionally grounded checks on partisan abuses and deal a severe blow to representative democracy. We can't let that happen on our watch.
The vote suppressors will keep testing the limits of their power and these obscure, fringe theories as long as they can in order to protect their own power. Stopping them will take a lot of work and a strong response at the ballot box in a few months.
Chip in to push back on the vote suppressors and their fringe theories with $35 or whatever you can. Together, we can inform voters and turn them out to protect our democracy! >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=022526_1&amount=35]

# **Trump celebrates "transformation like no one has ever seen" in record-breaking State of the Union**
President Donald Trump delivered his first State of the Union address of his second term Tuesday evening, celebrating what he called a "turnaround for the ages" after "just one year" in office. The speech broke records as the longest in recent history, focusing on snuffing out DEI policies, securing the border, unleashing U.S. energy, and bolstering the economy with savings for working families through no tax on tips or overtime.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/7bf7750c-020a-474b-8edb-81a105060921?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Sarah Beckstrom, 20, who was fatally injured during a terror attack in Washington, D.C.

# **Mother of murdered Ukrainian refugee breaks down as Trump recounts brutal killing during State of the Union**
Anna Zarutska, mother of murdered Ukrainian refugee Iryna Zarutska, **[broke down in tears during President Trump's State of the Union address](https://substack.com/redirect/fdfb858e-e4f8-4080-a479-3f14bda70d1b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as he recounted how her 22-year-old daughter was fatally stabbed by repeat offender Decarlos Brown on a Charlotte, North Carolina light rail train in August. Trump described how Brown "viciously slashed a knife through her neck and body," saying Iryna "had escaped a brutal war only to be slain by a hardened criminal, set free to kill in America."

Musk explained: **_“That’s why they want open borders... That’s why some leaders changed their views on borders. That’s the reason—to bring in more people who could affect our systems.”_**

## Hey, My Angry Democrats and My Angry Patriots.
Last night was the State of the Union address from President Donald Trump. I'll be honest, I'm not a big fan of watching these speeches live. They're always packed with political theater, and half the time I'm not even yelling at the TV because of what the President is saying, I'm yelling because of what Congress is doing: who shows up, who doesn't, what they jump up to clap for, what they refuse to acknowledge, and how performative it all gets while I'm trying to focus on the substance.
So instead, I usually wait until the next morning, go to the sources and commentators from different sides of the aisle, and watch their breakdowns while and search for fact-checks of the biggest claims. That's what I did today, and it pushed me to compile everything into one place so readers of **The Angry Democrat** can quickly scan the major fact checks without chasing a dozen tabs.
These are pulled from a variety of outlets, **and I used AI (Chat GPT & Grok to fact check Chat GPT)** to put them into a single, readable post. The original sources are included so you can dig in and verify the details yourself. I hope this helps you understand what was said, what holds up, what doesn't, and what deserves more scrutiny.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/2833f29e-f834-4b8f-939c-e1438ea8a1e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
## 1) I inherited a stagnant economy with inflation at record levels.
Rating: false
Multiple fact-checks dispute this framing. FactCheck.org says real GDP growth was solid during the prior administration and inflation had already cooled substantially before Trump took office, making "stagnant" and "record levels" inaccurate as a description of what he inherited. ([FactCheck.org](https://substack.com/redirect/31f972ff-2071-4987-8625-370267bd32b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
AP similarly reports Trump's "inherited disaster" framing doesn't match the underlying trend lines they cite for growth and inflation coming into his term. ([AP News](https://substack.com/redirect/34ee77d2-90a0-4ac6-91c4-18f369eb41cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 2) The economy is roaring like never before.
Rating: mostly false / hyperbolic
Several outlets characterize this as an exaggeration rather than a measurable claim. FactCheck.org notes the relevant indicators don't support "like never before" in a literal sense and emphasizes that job growth and other measures aren't unprecedented. ([FactCheck.org](https://substack.com/redirect/31f972ff-2071-4987-8625-370267bd32b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
NBC's fact-check roundup likewise frames the "best-ever/never-before" language as overstated compared with typical economic baselines and population growth effects. ([NBC Chicago](https://substack.com/redirect/507f127a-e565-4ddc-aa00-ccddb9c0abfb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 3) Inflation is plummeting / Prices are plummeting downward.
Rating: misleading
Fact-checkers consistently draw the distinction between **inflation falling** (rate of increase slowing) and **prices falling** (deflation). NPR's annotated fact-check says inflation has cooled, but that doesn't mean broad prices are "plummeting." ([WVTN](https://substack.com/redirect/bbf154b8-f2ef-4545-af0d-9ef43d71da33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
AP also flags similar rhetoric as misleading because it implies prices are dropping across the board. ([AP News](https://substack.com/redirect/34ee77d2-90a0-4ac6-91c4-18f369eb41cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 4) Gas is now below $2.30 in most states... I saw $1.85 in Iowa.
Rating: mostly false
Independent checks say the "most states" claim doesn't match statewide averages and the very low price anecdotes aren't representative. The Guardian's fact-check summary reports averages were higher than claimed and treats the assertion as inflated. ([The Guardian](https://substack.com/redirect/ca94c947-3ad1-4182-9fd1-8cdde548b8f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
AP likewise includes gas-price claims among Trump's false or misleading statements in its fact-check writeup. ([AP News](https://substack.com/redirect/34ee77d2-90a0-4ac6-91c4-18f369eb41cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 5) Worst inflation in the history of our country.
Rating: false
NPR's annotated fact-check explicitly rejects "worst in history," noting inflation reached a modern-era high but not an all-time historical peak. ([WVTN](https://substack.com/redirect/bbf154b8-f2ef-4545-af0d-9ef43d71da33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
FactCheck.org also rejects the "worst in history" line and references historical periods with higher inflation rates. ([FactCheck.org](https://substack.com/redirect/31f972ff-2071-4987-8625-370267bd32b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 6) The stock market set 53 all-time record highs... everybody's up, way up.
Rating: mixed / misleading
Even when indices hit records, "everybody's up" is not accurate in distributional terms. NPR points out stock ownership is concentrated, so market gains don't translate evenly across households. ([WVTN](https://substack.com/redirect/bbf154b8-f2ef-4545-af0d-9ef43d71da33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
CBS also treats the "everybody" framing as misleading and adds context about who benefits from market rises. ([CBS News](https://substack.com/redirect/5d1204f2-eaa4-4718-9312-90d4efc3d79d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 7) More Americans are working today than at any time in history" and "100% of jobs created under my administration have been private-sector.
Rating: mostly true headline, but misleading implication
Fact-checkers typically treat the raw "most people working" metric as mechanically true in many years because population grows, but misleading as proof of exceptional performance. FactCheck.org notes the population-growth problem and comparisons to recent years. ([FactCheck.org](https://substack.com/redirect/31f972ff-2071-4987-8625-370267bd32b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
Hearst/PolitiFact partner writeups (carried by local affiliates) make the same point: the statement is "misleading" because employment tends to rise over time absent recessions. ([KCRA](https://substack.com/redirect/a137c809-4894-4a2d-8c55-7024ca3f73a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 8) Largest tax cuts in American history.
Rating: false
NPR's annotated fact-check says analyses do not support "largest in history," describing it as an overclaim relative to other major tax cuts. ([WVTN](https://substack.com/redirect/bbf154b8-f2ef-4545-af0d-9ef43d71da33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
CBS likewise does not rate it as the largest historically when providing context around the claim. ([CBS News](https://substack.com/redirect/5d1204f2-eaa4-4718-9312-90d4efc3d79d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 9) No tax on tips, no tax on overtime, no tax on Social Security.
Rating: misleading / partly true
Multiple sources describe the "no tax" slogan as oversimplified because eligibility limits and carve-outs apply, and because implementation details matter (caps, phase-outs, temporary provisions, etc.). FactCheck.org treats the blanket phrasing as misleading without the fine print. ([FactCheck.org](https://substack.com/redirect/31f972ff-2071-4987-8625-370267bd32b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
CBS similarly frames these as narrower than the slogan implies. ([CBS News](https://substack.com/redirect/5d1204f2-eaa4-4718-9312-90d4efc3d79d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 10) Tariffs are paid for by foreign countries and will replace income tax.
Rating: mostly false
NPR's annotated fact-check states economists generally find tariffs are paid largely by U.S. importers/consumers (not "foreign countries" in the way claimed), and it treats "replace income tax" as not realistic on the math. ([WVTN](https://substack.com/redirect/bbf154b8-f2ef-4545-af0d-9ef43d71da33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
FactCheck.org likewise calls the "replace income taxes" framing dubious and not supported by standard economic analysis. ([FactCheck.org](https://substack.com/redirect/31f972ff-2071-4987-8625-370267bd32b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 11) Strongest and most secure border in American history.
Rating: partly true / not provable as "in history"
There is evidence of historically low encounter levels in the modern data series, but "in history" is broader than what the data can prove. Pew Research reports encounters at the U.S.-Mexico border are at their lowest level in more than 50 years (based on available monthly data), which supports the "very low" direction of the claim. ([Pew Research Center](https://substack.com/redirect/06c57018-25e3-4e84-805c-0a9d47f00f77?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
DHS messaging also claims the "most secure border," but as a political assertion rather than an independently verified historical statement. ([Department of Homeland Security](https://substack.com/redirect/ac3db207-3a66-48d0-8417-ddfde6c621f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 12) Biden had it wide open, unvetted.
Rating: misleading
Fact-checkers reject "wide open" and "unvetted" as blanket characterizations, noting there were vetting processes in multiple programs and policy tightening over time. NPR's annotated fact-check directly disputes the "unvetted" framing. ([WVTN](https://substack.com/redirect/bbf154b8-f2ef-4545-af0d-9ef43d71da33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
AP also treats this type of broad-brush claim as misleading in its recap of false and misleading assertions. ([AP News](https://substack.com/redirect/34ee77d2-90a0-4ac6-91c4-18f369eb41cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 13) They poured in by the millions from prisons and mental institutions...
Rating: unsupported
Multiple fact-checkers describe this as lacking evidence. NPR's annotated fact-check says there is no evidence for the "prisons/mental institutions" narrative at the scale implied. ([WVTN](https://substack.com/redirect/bbf154b8-f2ef-4545-af0d-9ef43d71da33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
AP includes similar "they're emptying prisons/mental institutions" assertions in its broader set of misinformation flags. ([AP News](https://substack.com/redirect/34ee77d2-90a0-4ac6-91c4-18f369eb41cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 14) Cheating is rampant in our elections.
Rating: false
Multiple sources reiterate that verified fraud rates are very low and that "rampant" is inconsistent with available evidence. RNZ's fact-check writeup directly states there's no basis for describing U.S. elections as broadly "rampant" with cheating and notes fraud is a tiny fraction of votes. ([RNZ](https://substack.com/redirect/93ddedcd-35b6-4765-ac05-c4eb99b0d018?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
FactCheck.org similarly says Trump repeats "rampant" claims without evidence and references extensive prior reviews and court outcomes that did not validate widespread fraud claims. ([FactCheck.org](https://substack.com/redirect/31f972ff-2071-4987-8625-370267bd32b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 15) I secured commitments for more than $18 trillion pouring in.
Rating: unsubstantiated / likely inflated
Multiple outlets characterize the figure as not supported by transparent, verifiable commitments at that scale. The Guardian reports outside tallies and the White House's own accounting do not align with $18T and describes the figure as inflated by pledges that may not materialize. ([The Guardian](https://substack.com/redirect/ca94c947-3ad1-4182-9fd1-8cdde548b8f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
FactCheck.org also calls it unsubstantiated and notes missing detail and the inclusion of non-binding or uncertain pledges. ([FactCheck.org](https://substack.com/redirect/31f972ff-2071-4987-8625-370267bd32b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 16) We obliterated Iran's nuclear program.
Rating: overstated / not verifiable as claimed
NPR's annotated fact-check says damage assessments are uncertain without inspection access and treats "obliterated" as overclaiming certainty and completeness. ([WVTN](https://substack.com/redirect/bbf154b8-f2ef-4545-af0d-9ef43d71da33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
FactCheck.org similarly characterizes "obliterated" as stronger than what can be responsibly confirmed from available evidence. ([FactCheck.org](https://substack.com/redirect/31f972ff-2071-4987-8625-370267bd32b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 17) In my first 10 months, I ended eight wars.
Rating: exaggerated
The Guardian's fact-check summary disputes the count and the definition of "wars," noting some ceasefires were temporary and some situations cited are not typically categorized as wars. ([The Guardian](https://substack.com/redirect/ca94c947-3ad1-4182-9fd1-8cdde548b8f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
AP likewise treats the claim as inflated in its roundup of misleading statements. ([AP News](https://substack.com/redirect/34ee77d2-90a0-4ac6-91c4-18f369eb41cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 18) We can balance the budget if we find enough fraud.
Rating: false / implausible
FactCheck.org argues the scale doesn't work: annual deficit figures are far larger than credible estimates of recoverable fraud. ([FactCheck.org](https://substack.com/redirect/31f972ff-2071-4987-8625-370267bd32b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
CBS similarly treats the "fraud alone balances the budget" argument as not adding up when compared with deficit magnitude. ([CBS News](https://substack.com/redirect/5d1204f2-eaa4-4718-9312-90d4efc3d79d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 19) Americans will now pay the lowest price anywhere in the world for prescription drugs (via TrumpRx/MFN framing)
Rating: mostly false / overstated
NPR's annotated fact-check disputes the "lowest anywhere in the world" claim and describes limitations in scope and how most insured patients pay (copays/coverage dynamics). ([WVTN](https://substack.com/redirect/bbf154b8-f2ef-4545-af0d-9ef43d71da33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
FactCheck.org also treats the claim as unsupported at the broad level implied and emphasizes that program constraints undercut the universal phrasing. ([FactCheck.org](https://substack.com/redirect/31f972ff-2071-4987-8625-370267bd32b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 20) Trump accounts could grow to $100,000 by age 18.
Rating: highly optimistic
Multiple fact-check writeups treat this as a best-case, assumption-heavy projection rather than a likely outcome. ABC News' fact-check package frames similar "could reach" projections as dependent on strong market returns and consistent contributions, making the implied certainty misleading. ([ABC7 Los Angeles](https://substack.com/redirect/4af26d84-e65f-4879-9ecc-72c52103bef2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
FactCheck.org also treats the $100,000 number as not a grounded expectation for typical assumptions. ([FactCheck.org](https://substack.com/redirect/31f972ff-2071-4987-8625-370267bd32b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 21) Unemployment remains low by historical standards.
**Rating: true**
Economic reporting confirms the unemployment rate remains relatively low (e.g., ~4.3% in early 2026), indicating a comparatively strong labor market even if job growth has slowed. Reuters data on weekly jobless claims supports labor market stability despite concerns. ([Nevada Public Radio](https://substack.com/redirect/1e9ba24b-14b9-4abd-a254-11166ccb2f78?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 22) The U.S. economy has added jobs in each year of my administration.
**Rating: true**
Though job gains slowed in 2025, employment levels continued to rise, consistent with Trump's claim that the net number of jobs did not decline year-over-year. Fact-checkers note job creation continued through 2025, even if slower than prior years. ([Nevada Public Radio](https://substack.com/redirect/1e9ba24b-14b9-4abd-a254-11166ccb2f78?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 23) Border encounters have fallen from recent highs.
**Rating: true**
Though Trump's absolute "zero" claim is false, ABC News and other outlets acknowledge that encounters at the U.S. border have dropped significantly from earlier peaks, supporting the basic directional assertion of a reduction. ([ABC News](https://substack.com/redirect/4a550196-76b7-4c39-9dde-a774d547ac16?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 24) Service members received the $1,776 'warrior dividend' checks.
**Rating: true**
Despite disagreement on the funding source, multiple outlets confirmed that the government disbursed the promised $1,776 payments to eligible military personnel as he described. ([facebook.com](https://substack.com/redirect/9f14f2b3-46e0-4b25-8d54-bc780c7b301a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 25) "The stock market has seen record highs for major indexes."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/76dac872-6f9b-4062-929c-0a0d98019dbf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Rating: true**
Reuters reported that major U.S. stock indices (including the Dow and S&P 500) reached significant record levels under Trump's second term, which supports his broader point about market performance boosting retirement savings. ([Reuters](https://substack.com/redirect/296917c2-bcec-4694-8eb9-3c8c7239697c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* * *
## 26) He delivered the longest State of the Union address in U.S. history.
**Rating: true**
Multiple reports confirm Trump's address on February 24, 2026, lasted about **1 hour and 48 minutes,** making it the longest formally designated State of the Union ever recorded, surpassing previous records
