Hey folks,
I sat down with **Simon Rosenberg** today--and if you've been feeling like the ground is shifting under Trump, you're not crazy. The numbers are brutal. The map is expanding. And for the first time in a long time, it feels like _they 're_ the ones on defense. We broke down the polling, the Senate battlefield, the Epstein scandal metastasizing in real time, and why the GOP's entire strategy right now feels like a panic spiral.
**Here 's what we got into:**
* [**00:01:12**] We dig into Trump's collapsing approval numbers--36% approval, 26% with independents--and why he's fallen faster than he did before the 2018 blue wave.
* [**00:08:58**] The Senate map suddenly looks competitive in places that would've been "unimaginable" a year ago--Ohio, Iowa, Alaska, Texas--and why the GOP's mid-decade gerrymander backfired.
* [**00:14:57**] Simon lays out why the Epstein scandal may be more destabilizing than anything else on the board--and how legitimacy, not just polling, is now at stake.
* [**00:21:49**] We talk tariffs, the looming budget hole, and why Democrats should be running on refund checks with interest--because Trump just forced Republicans to vote for price hikes.
* [**00:30:08**] I explain what I'm seeing on Fox, Newsmax, and the Daily Wire: they look weaker. Shakier. On the run. The swagger is gone.

The big takeaway? When we fight, we win. When we expose the harm, we expand the map. When we organize, we outperform. We have to block the harms. We have to prosecute the case. body:

Mark Levin just went nuclear, and he asked a question we can no longer ignore:
| | | | |
---
Dear Faithful Friend,
Mark Levin just went nuclear, and he asked a question we can no longer ignore: **
**_**"You ready, America?"**_
**Because what's happening in Texas isn't just a state issue anymore – it’s becoming Ground Zero in the battle for Western civilization.** _
_**All across Europe, countries are rapidly losing their identities as a result of unfettered mass migration with no assimilation.** **
** Parallel societies have begun to emerge and they are incompatible – one based upon Western, Judeo-Christian values, and one based upon Sharia Law, or Islamic Law.
**You could say this is just a European problem, but Sharia is the primary driver of Christian persecution across the planet, and it’s begun to gain a foothold right here in America.** **_
_** On a recent show, a retired Texas police lieutenant blew the whistle directly to Levin._**He revealed details about EPIC City – a proposed Sharia-compliant "Islamic mega-city" being planned on roughly 400 acres in Texas.** Critics claim it's designed to function separately from American society, operating under Sharia principles rather than U.S. law._ _
___Mark's response was unequivocal:__ __
______**“Sharia Law has no place in the United States of America.”**____ ____**
**____ And yet, other shocking examples keep coming, including Sharia materials and hijabs (veils) being distributed in some Texas schools.
**Now it’s time for citizens to have their say, because on March 3rd, Texas Republicans will vote on a ballot initiative declaring "Texas should ban Sharia Law."** **
** In the lead-up to this vote, political leaders in Texas have been fighting hard:
* Governor Greg Abbott has designated CAIR and the Muslim Brotherhood as foreign terrorist organizations.
* Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick urged Texas Senate committees to make preventing Sharia law influence a top priority for possible 2027 legislation.
* Attorney General Ken Paxton is investigating Islamic developments for violations of Texas law.
* U.S. Congressmen Keith Self and Chip Roy launched the Sharia-Free America Caucus with 33 members from 18 states.

| **When Headlines Tell the Story of "Republicans" Who Vote with Democrats to Raise Taxes, We Have a Problem**
---
| You may have thought our fellow "conservative Republicans" would know that we are not supposed to raise taxes, but apparently not everyone agrees with us. Our opponent, Kevin Wilson, joined with Democrats in Adams County and voted to increase property taxes up to 30%. He was President of the Board at the time, and [led the vote to a unanimous 5-0 tax increase](https://voteroneller.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=cadf08ca3f7559848c17d00e3&id=e2364bd449&e=a56613e05b).

Mr. Wilson is the only Republican on the Adams County Board of Supervisors. If we can't trust him to stand for Republican values with his neighbors in Adams County, how does anyone think he can stand up to the lobbyists, cronies, and political hacks in Washington DC?

Mr. Wilson even gave a speech about why RAISING taxes was necessary because of a budget shortfall that happened under his watch as President of the Board. He doesn’t want to admit that they didn’t watch the money being spent for an entire year and then found out they were $4 million in the hole. Does that sound like a responsible watchdog over your taxpayer dollars??

Republicans need to take out Bennie Thompson, but replacing him with another reckless tax and spend Republican isn't making a change in DC. [That's why Ron Eller signed the Taxpayer Protection Pledge from the Americans for Tax Reform.](https://voteroneller.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=cadf08ca3f7559848c17d00e3&id=4d20936625&e=a56613e05b) He pledges to NEVER raise your taxes.

We know who the REAL conservative running for Congress in Mississippi's District Two is. ### **_Stand for Health Freedom endorses Ron Eller for Congress_****.**
Stand for Health Freedom has endorsed conservative Republican Ron Eller for the Second Congressional District of Mississippi. With the Republican primary just days away on March 10, Eller is again receiving the support of conservative activists nationwide against his primary opponent.

Eller, a Physician’s Assistant in Jackson, expressed his gratitude for the endorsement: “It is my great honor to receive Stand for Health Freedom's endorsement. I have long respected this highly effective advocacy organization for its stalwart defender of individual liberty and health freedom.”

Like Stand for Health Freedom, Eller has consistently advocated individual freedom of choice and opposed vaccine and mask mandates and centralized government control over health care. Eller stated, “Stand for Health Freedom supports candidates who make and support policy to protect and expand individual and family choice in matters of personal health. I will defend and expand these rights for Mississippi residents.”

Leah Wilson, Executive Director of Stand for Health Freedom, says, “We are seeing an increasing number of medical professionals and physicians prioritize health freedom. They see the value in protecting each individual in order to have a community of healthy and free individuals. Eller is a shining example and will represent Mississippi with the backbone and principles that are needed to fix what’s broken in Washington.”

Stand for Health Freedom (SHF) endorses political candidates who prioritize individual liberty, medical freedom, and informed consent. These endorsements highlight a commitment to reducing government overreach in personal healthcare decisions. Key themes of endorsed candidates often include:

**Medical Freedom:** Protecting the right to make personal health decisions without government mandates.

**Informed Consent:** Ensuring transparency and personal choice in medical treatments.

**Legislative Action:** Opposing government overreach and defending constitutional rights.

But instead of a clear plan to lower costs or keep our communities safe, we got more of the same: fearmongering, finger-pointing, and a vision completely out of touch with real life. clean_body: | = Friend, Yesterday, I sat in the House chamber and listened closely as President Trump addressed the country. I came with one goal: to represent Southern California families looking for real solutions, not more political showmanship. But instead of a clear plan to lower costs or keep our communities safe, we got more of the same: fearmongering, finger-pointing, and a vision completely out of touch with real life. At a time when small businesses are fighting to stay open, families are stretched thin by rising costs, and trust in government is near a breaking point -- we need leadership rooted in reality, not rhetoric. I’ll work with anyone, Republican or Democrat, who’s serious about making life more affordable, safer, and more just. Whether it’s fighting to lower health care costs or holding agencies like ICE accountable when they violate the public’s trust, I’ve stayed focused on the work that actually improves lives. clean_body: Last night, Trump gave his State of the Union address. | | | | Last night, Trump gave his State of the Union address. I did not attend because I refuse to normalize Trump's parade of lies and attempts to tighten his authoritarian grip. Instead, I held a "Fate of the Union" discussion with Senator Wyden to take questions from citizens across the state. In the last year, Trump has made America sicker and poorer. His so-called "Big, Beautiful Bill" was a Big, Ugly BETRAYAL of working families. Programs families count on for health care and nutrition assistance have been gutted. Millions are left without the support they need to survive — let alone get ahead. And for what? To fund tax breaks for billionaires. Trump's Big, Ugly Betrayal was one of the largest transfers of wealth from working people to wealthy people in a single bill in our nation's history. Families lose. Billionaires win. That's the agenda. That's what he wanted us to celebrate. I won't. At the same time, we're watching unaccountable ICE operations cause chaos in our communities — deadly actions, little transparency, and families living in constant anxiety. We need to reject this families lose, billionaires win mentality and build a country where families thrive and billionaires finally pay their fair share. Peter,

Last night, Donald Trump took the stage and did what he does best: lie.

He bragged about an economy that working families don’t recognize, while
costs are still rising, rent is too high, groceries are squeezing
paychecks, and millions of people are just trying to stay afloat.

He boasted about his so-called “crime crackdown,” praising the armed
deployment of the National Guard into our communities. We know what that
really means. Innocent people harmed and communities destabilized and
damaged.

He claimed foreign policy “victories,” while escalating tensions that
bring us closer to war with Iran, interfering in Venezuela, and turning a
blind eye to the genocide unfolding in Gaza.

Trump is a walking contradiction. But he is dangerous all the same. If the
last year is a preview of what’s to come, we cannot afford to sit on the
sidelines.

That’s why Alexandria, Ayanna, Ilhan, and Rashida are doing what they
always do: standing unapologetically with the people. They are speaking
truth to power, demanding accountability, and organizing for justice on
all fronts.

The Squad Victory Fund exists to have their backs in fights exactly like
this — helping power their actions, amplifying their voices, and building
the grassroots strength it takes to confront extremism head-on.

Now we need to meet this moment. If you believe we cannot allow another
year of family separations, war threats, and unchecked cruelty, if you
believe someone has to stand up and say “enough,” then this is your moment
to step into the fight.

subject: Young People’s State of the Union
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
This is what our generation is actually facing.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260225-1&t=1&akid=3185%2E587540%2Ej2xhS0)
Peter,
Last night, President Trump gave his State of the Union.
I’m sure you’ve seen by now that he said a lot of crazy stuff. That’s not surprising. That’s not what this email is about, either. I want to talk about what he left unsaid.
Last night was a clear demonstration that our government is painfully out of step with young people. Politicians like Donald Trump don’t understand the issues we’re facing. They don’t even pretend to care about solutions to those problems.
What I didn’t hear in last night’s speech was how the government is going to work for young people — the ones who are going to inherit the mess being made in Washington.
I want everyone to know what it’s really like for young people in this country today.
**So here’s the Young People’s State of the Union:**
**We grew up practicing active shooter drills before we learned algebra.**
School shootings have increased dramatically in the last decade, with more school shooting incidents in recent years than any previous generation experienced in K-12. The average member of Congress did not grow up in an era where school shooting drills were routine. Columbine happened in 1999 — many current lawmakers were already adults.
**We scroll past climate disasters like they’re weather updates.**
The U.S. now experiences an average of 20+ billion-dollar climate disasters per year — compared to fewer than 5 annually in the 1980s. Gen Z will live through significantly more extreme heat waves and climate disasters than previous generations, even under moderate warming scenarios.
**We work full-time and still can’t afford rent — let alone a home.**
In 1980, the median home cost about 2–3x the median household income. Today, it’s closer to 5–6x in many markets. Homeownership rates for young adults today are significantly lower than they were for Baby Boomers and Gen X at the same age. A full-time minimum wage worker cannot afford a two-bedroom rental anywhere in the United States at fair market rent.
**We’re drowning in student debt for degrees we were told we had to get.**
Outstanding student loan debt now exceeds $1.7 trillion. The average borrower leaves school with tens of thousands in debt — far more (adjusted for inflation) than previous generations. In the 1970s, tuition at public universities was a fraction of today’s cost relative to income. AND even when young people graduate college they now face over 40% unemployment for recent graduates.
**Our mental health is in crisis.**
Rates of anxiety and depression among young adults have surged over the last decade. Suicide is now one of the leading causes of death for young people. Young people report significantly higher rates of loneliness and hopelessness than previous generations at the same age.
**We’re navigating an internet that shapes our lives faster than it can be regulated.**
Nearly half of teens report being online “almost constantly.” Social media use is strongly correlated with increased mental health challenges among adolescents, especially young women. Lawmakers crafting tech policy largely did not grow up in the digital ecosystem they’re regulating.
**Even when we do everything “right,” finding a good-paying job feels out of reach.**
Young workers’ wages have not kept pace with housing, healthcare, and education costs. Entry-level jobs increasingly require degrees and experience that previous generations weren’t expected to have. Many Gen Z workers report feeling financially worse off than their parents were at the same age.
**I’ve had enough, Peter.** It’s time for leaders who are actually on our side. That’s what we’re doing here at Leaders We Deserve — electing a new generation that understands what’s at stake and refuses to back down from fighting for our future. We know that what young voters care about far more than Party ID is lived experience and feeling like those in power actually understand what they are going through. There is no better way of doing that than electing young people who, for example, unlike most members of Congress, have actually paid rent in the 21st century.
**[If you believe young people deserve leaders who understand what they’re up against, will you pitch in $5 to help us elect the next generation?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260225_1_sotu.6IRaHf&refcode=em20260225-3185&amount=5&t=2&akid=3185%2E587540%2Ej2xhS0)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260225_1_sotu.6IRaHf&amount=5&refcode=em20260225-3185&t=21&akid=3185%2E587540%2Ej2xhS0)**
Peter, our candidates learned active shooter drills. They are paying off student loans. They know what it’s like to apply for 100 jobs and not hear back from any.
These are the kinds of leaders we need in power. But we have to be honest: This system wasn’t built for them. It was built for people with money and connections.
That’s why it’s so vital that we invest in these races and uplift these young leaders. Often, we are the biggest contributors to their campaigns. Our support can mean the difference between a victory and a loss in a tight race. We’ve seen it happen.
We’ve already elected 3 candidates this cycle. With one of them winning by just 153 votes to become the youngest lawmaker in Georgia's history. We’re supporting more than a dozen more, with more endorsements on the way. We aren’t slowing down.
But that means we need your support more than ever. We can’t do this alone.
**[If you can, will you make a $5 donation to power this movement?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260225_1_sotu.6IRaHf&refcode=em20260225-3185&amount=5&t=22&akid=3185%2E587540%2Ej2xhS0)**
The real State of the Union for young people is complicated. It’s frustrating.
But it’s also full of potential — if we’re willing to organize for it and invest in it.
Let’s build the future we deserve.
Thank you,
David Hogg

subject: As a retired general, I know: War in Iran will cost American lives
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY VOTEVETS ACTION FUND
body:
The question is: Do Trump and the GOP care?
#
Peter, Paul Eaton here.
It is no secret that the Trump administration wants a regime change war with Iran. After 25 years in the Army, I think I speak with some credibility when I tell you this: Trump is in no way ready for that war and the casualties it could bring.
[**VoteVets just launched our Substack, and I’ve written our first entry about the danger Trump is exposing our troops to by leading them into this conflict. I am humbly asking you to give it a read.**](https://act.votevets.org/go/19669?triedRedirect=true%3Frefcode%3Dem260225-2-PE&t=1&akid=34967%2E3013755%2EqCIahS)
| [War in Iran
Will Cost American Lives](https://act.votevets.org/go/19669?triedRedirect=true%3Frefcode%3Dem260225-2-PE&t=2&akid=34967%2E3013755%2EqCIahS)
---
Behind closed doors, Trump’s own handpicked Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff has warned about the complexity of a major Iran operation, the risk of U.S. casualties, and the strain created by depleted U.S. munitions and missile-defense interceptor stocks.
I share his assessment. There are 40,000 troops across Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan, Syria, Qatar, and other regional sites. If Tehran believes that Washington is threatening the regime’s survival, the safest assumption is that they will hit back, hard and fast, at the most obvious targets: Our bases and our troops. Make no mistake: an attack on Iran would be a war of choice.
I watched Iraq descend into chaos and bloodshed because the mission had no realistic political end state, no metrics for when it could end. The American people should demand that a decision this grave be debated in the open, with clear objectives, a defined end state, and an exit plan.
**Congress must vote on a War Powers Resolution.**
[**If you’d like to hear more from this old soldier about the threats young Americans will be exposed to and the absolute necessity of a War Powers Resolution, use this link and read on.**](https://act.votevets.org/signup/2602018_MK_Event_030326/?refcode=em260225-2-PE&t=3&akid=34967%2E3013755%2EqCIahS)
Thank you,
Paul Eaton
Major General, U.S. Army, Retired
Senior Advisor, VoteVets
